messages:
maria: quick brain dump on dedicated GPU pool autoscaling. leaning to hybrid: local fast-path for tiny spikes, global allocator for large bursts and fairness. want to flush tradeoffs before RFC follow-up. :spiral_calendar:
ryan: sounds good. local = low latency; central = global view + easier cross-pool bursting. main risk is coordination surface.
sophia: please enumerate bad states: double-prewarm, quota blowout, noisy tenant causing churn. ops needs clear invariants.
todd: ops note: more local controllers = more things to debug; central = single PI if it flaps. need graceful degraded modes.
anya: hybrid sketch: local token cache for sub-second prewarms; central issues leases for heavier capacity. tokens = cheap, leases = billable/accounted.
ryan: central->local API minimal surface: grant_capacity(tenant, n, ttl, lease_id) and revoke(lease_id). keep it skinny.
maria: agree. invariants proposal: central is authoritative for committed reservations; local may consume tokens up to local_budget; anything above requires central lease; revokes honored within revoke_grace_ms or alarm.
sophia: config sketch (example):
```
poolPolicy:
  localBudgetFraction: 0.06
  spareHeadroomPct: 0.05
  localSpinupMax: 4
  centralThreshold: 4
```
keeps microbursts local.
todd: central allocator will see lagging metrics. be conservative in grants to avoid oversubscribe.
anya: token-bucket idea: locals draw tokens for quick prewarms; central replenishes tokens periodically using short-term forecast + safe margin. tokens cheaper than lease RPCs.
maria: accounting rule: tokens_in_use + active_leases <= physical_gpus - reserved_capacity. locals must report tokens_left metric.
sophia: partition case: if central unreachable, locals operate only within token budget and set central_stale=true metric; emit degraded-mode.
ryan: prewarm lifecycle states: requested -> warming -> ready -> in_use -> idle -> retired. idle entries carry lastUsedTs and warmCostEstimate. idle_ttl governs reclamation.
todd: eviction heuristic: score = a*idle_secs + b*warm_cost_ms - c*tenant_priority; evict highest scores. prefer tenant-aware eviction over pure LRU.
anya: fairness: central maintains per-org burst_credits that replenish slowly. credits are decremented on lease/grant to throttle heavy spenders.
maria: fallback options when lease denied: queue, spin smaller model, route to hosted fallback, or 429. tenant-level policy selects behavior.
sophia: telemetry req: tag each admission with admission={local,token,lease,denied}, reason={headroom,quota,partition,error}, decision_ts, and lease_id when applicable.
ryan: rollout plan: 1) local token plugin PoC on non-prod pools, 2) central lease API dev, 3) A/B on small set of pools, 4) add revoke/preempt + accounting, 5) wider rollout.
maria: API surface for RFC: request_tokens(n), request_lease(n, ttl, priority), extend_lease(id, ttl), revoke_lease(id), status. locals configured with localBudgetFraction.
anya: TTLs should default short and be extendable with an extend_lease call. avoids long-lived forgotten leases.
todd: testing: chaos (central partition), noisy-tenant storms, cross-region simultaneous bursts, eviction fairness runs. also cost regression checks.
ryan: ops fallback: if central overloaded, switch to tokens-only mode with tightened headroom and alert. ensure fail-open policy doesn't oversubscribe physical GPUs.
sophia: docs: sequence diagrams for grant, revoke, partition failover, and tenant-deny path. include error codes for lease RPCs and retry semantics.
maria: action items: ryan -> prototype central lease API this sprint; sophia -> draft invariants + metrics; anya -> PoC token-bucket local plugin; todd -> define chaos scenarios and SLO gates. will schedule 30m sync after PoCs land. thanks all :+1:
